text: Let's get Python installed on your machine. This lesson is hands-on — by the end, you'll have a working Python, a code editor, and your first virtual environment.

Download the installer from python.org/downloads — not a third-party site. There's one checkbox that trips up almost every beginner: Add python.exe to PATH. It's unchecked by default. Check it before clicking Install Now.
This course uses Visual Studio Code. Open the Extensions view, search python, and install the official Python extension from Microsoft — the one with the blue checkmark and millions of installs.

Next, a virtual environment — an isolated copy of Python just for one project. Create it with python -m venv .venv, then use VS Code's Select Interpreter command to point the editor at it — marked Recommended once found.
Confirm everything's connected by actually running a file. VS Code's terminal shows exactly which python.exe ran your script — here it's the one inside .venv — and the real output underneath.
With Python installed, confirmed, and a virtual environment ready, the actual language starts next lesson: variables and data types.
